The SuperUnicode® Standard

Version 0.1.0 — the native character encoding of the OpenWindows kernel.

SuperUnicode defines the character system, machine instructions and storage framing that the OpenWindows kernel speaks natively. It is organized as two complementary systems:

  • Base SUCS — a 31-bit space (0x00000000–0x7FFFFFFF) that is 1:1 compatible with Unicode in its low range, carries its own System Control Plane of machine instructions, and reserves a vast native space for OpenWindows codepoints.
  • ExtSUCS (SuperUnicode Extended) — an unbounded, 64-bit space beyond the Base ceiling. New codepoints are added by plugins that mount as read-only OWFS partitions after a boot-time checksum gate.

What does “native” mean? Every string, filename and data file in OpenWindows is a SuperUnicode stream by default. The kernel renders it directly — no transcoding step, no code-page table. Storage (OWFS/USFS), framing (SUTF) and diagnostics (the SCP) are all defined by the same standard.

How the space is organized

Unicode Compatibility Space

0x000000 – 0x10FFFF

1:1 with Unicode, forever — even when Unicode publishes new versions or codepoints.

System Control Plane

0x110000 – 0x11FFFF

Machine instructions. Hosts the BANcode Registry (diagnostics, WARN/COM/SOFT codes).

Native SuperUnicode Space

0x120000 – 0x7FFFFFFF

OpenWindows’ own allocations. Above it, plugins extend the space without limit.
